isolation_mode.description: §2.1 (ADR-0018): `per_team` = one container instance per team, created at that team's challenge start and removed at its teardown. `shared` = one instance per event, shared by all teams - an opt-in valid only for games that can prove team isolation (§3.4 check 11); registry admission additionally refuses `shared` for privilege-escalation/arbitrary-code-execution games. The contract endpoints are identical in both modes.

provision_identity.description: §2.1: `handles` = /provision carries opaque ids and framework-generated handles only. `names` = the game additionally receives team_name, players[].username and players[].display_name; declaring it is a stated data-processing capability - justified in the registry submission, visible in the event's privacy notice, covered by teardown/logging tests (ADR-0019).

solve_mode.description: §2.1/§5: how a solve reaches the framework. `flag` = the game displays a produced `token` reward and the player submits it in the framework UI, so the solver is identified. `callback` = the game detects the win itself and calls the solved callback; use it only when there is nothing to paste. A manifest declaring a non-empty tcp_ports must use `flag` (§3.4 check 12).

ociImageRef.description: OCI image reference (§2.1): [registry[:port]/]path[/path...][:tag][@digest]. Path components are lowercase per the OCI distribution grammar; the registry host, tag and digest are all optional.
